standard_prerequisites.name: Invariance of the Fitting-ideal criterion under coordinate and generator change
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof freely change coordinates and regenerize the ideal I during the normalization steps, the pivot the whole argument rests on.

standard_prerequisites.name: The nodal quadratic model and reduced dimension-2 quotients
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-nodal-algebraic and lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies side (1), the completed nodal quadric, and the structure theorem that an ideal in a two-variable power series ring defining a reduced quotient is generated by one element.

core_obligations: Direction (1) implies (2) and (3) (proof lines 4337-4344): change coordinates so that A/I = k[[x_{n-1}, x_n]] modulo a nondegenerate quadric, and compute the Jacobian matrix explicitly; its (n-1)-minors generate I + m_A, which gives both reducedness and depth 1.

Unit pivoting normalization (proof lines 4346-4372): as long as some partial derivative d f_j / d x_i is a unit, trade f_j and x_i between the generators of I and the regular system of parameters; iterating in finitely many steps reaches parameters x_1, ..., x_n and generators x_1, ..., x_t, f_{t+1}, ..., f_m of I with every remaining partial derivative in m_A.

Block-shape minor estimate (proof lines 4374-4384): the Jacobian of the normalized presentation is block triangular with an identity block and an m_A block, so every (n-1)-minor lies in m_A^{n-1-t}; the ideal of minors cannot contain 1, Nakayama excludes I = m_A and forces n - 1 - t at most 1, the invertible-minor cases exclude t = n and t = n - 1, hence t = n - 2.

Conclusion (proof lines 4384-4388): A/I is a quotient of k[[x_{n-1}, x_n]]; by lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2 the ideal is generated by x_1, ..., x_{n-2} and one series f, and the condition on the minors says exactly that the quadratic term of f is nondegenerate, i.e. A/I is as in case (1).
proof_roadmap: Prove (1) implies (2) and (3) first: normal form plus an explicit Jacobian computation.
Pivot unit partial derivatives into the parameter system until none remain, regenerizing I each time.
Read the block shape off the normalized presentation, bound the minors in m_A^{n-1-t}, and pin t = n - 2 with Nakayama and the invertible-minor exclusions.
Apply the reduced dimension-2 quotient lemma and translate the minor condition back into nondegeneracy of the quadratic term.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes the nodal quotients A/I of a formal power series ring through the (n-1)-minors of the Jacobian matrix (statement lines 4311-4330). The proof (lines 4332-4388) is a hands-on normal-form argument: the unit-pivoting loop that strips the presentation down to two variables, the block-triangular estimate placing every minor in m_A^{n-1-t}, and the pinch t = n - 2 from Nakayama together with the exclusion of the invertible-minor cases, closing with the structure theorem for reduced quotients of a two-variable power series ring. H2: every step is elementary, but the pivoting bookkeeping and the final index computation must be kept straight and no step can be replaced by a citation.
